passage: I am Vaibhav, and I was in the shop when I saw two toddlers by the toy shelf. Indu, about two, grabbed a red car out of another child's hands. He wailed. Her father knelt and said gently, "Say sorry, Indu." She muttered, "Sorry," and pushed the car back into the boy's hand, then patted his arm. I doubt she knew she had done wrong, but her hand was gentle.

qa.q: What did Indu take from the other child?
What does Indu's gentle pat after returning the car suggest, and what else could explain it?
qa.a: It suggests she wanted to make things better after her father's prompt. She may only have been copying, without understanding that she had upset the boy.

qa.q: What could Indu's father do next to help her learn?
qa.a: He can keep showing simple repair, like giving the toy back and offering a hug, and say the boy felt sad without heavy blame.

qa.q: How might the boy feel when Indu pats him?
qa.a: He may feel comforted to have his car back, but he might still feel upset for a while.

grounding: A toddler who grabbed a toy hands it back and gives a gentle gesture after a prompted sorry, showing early reparation.

passage: On Monday Tanvir, two, snatched a truck from his cousin. Sudha said, "Tanvir, sorry?" and he handed it back, looking at the floor. On Wednesday he grabbed a spoon from his cousin and, when she cried, gave it back and flung his arms round her, without any prompt. On Friday he took her cup again and only gave it back when Sudha reminded him. Sudha thought the giving back was growing, though the grabbing was not gone yet.

qa.q: What did Tanvir do on Wednesday when his cousin cried?
qa.a: He gave back the spoon and hugged her without being told.

qa.q: What might Tanvir have felt when he handed back the truck on Monday, and what else could explain it?
qa.a: He may have felt uneasy because Sudha's tone changed and his cousin was upset. He may also just have been following her instruction, without seeing his own fault.

qa.q: What could Sudha do to support Tanvir's progress?
qa.a: Sudha can keep prompting simply, notice warmly when he repairs, and not expect him to stop grabbing all at once. 🙂

qa.q: How might Tanvir's cousin experience these three days?
qa.a: She probably feels upset when things are taken, but the hug and returned toys tell her he cares.

grounding: A toddler offers a toy back or a hug after prompting, showing early reparation rather than understanding of fault.
